analysis.title: Southern Co. (SO): First Take: Q3 EPS Beat vs GSe/Consensus and increased 2026 guidance; GA election results in focus
key_insights: Southern Co reported adjusted 3Q26 EPS of $1.94, above the GS estimate of $1.72 and FactSet consensus of $1.71.
SO raised full year 2026 EPS guidance to $4.70 from the prior range of $4.50-$4.60. GSe was $4.63 before the update. The 8%-9% adjusted EPS growth guidance through 2028 was reiterated.
SO contracted an incremental 4 GW of large load customers in the quarter, bringing total contracted load to ~21 GW.
SO identified an additional $4bn of capex beyond the $81bn base capital plan, from gas infrastructure expansion and nuclear uprates.
Retail sales were strong across customer classes. Commercial grew 7.3% as data center load ramped, with data center sales up 52% YoY.
The EPS beat came from higher EPS at Georgia Power, Alabama Power, Southern Power, SO Gas and Parent. Mississippi Power was in line with GS estimates.
At the income statement level, net income was above GSe on revenues above forecast, partly offset by higher operating expenses, with help from higher other income.
GS sees increased political and regulatory risk following the Georgia election results, despite solid earnings execution and large load updates.
GS expects the call to focus on regulatory and policy implications after the elections, data center updates on the 21 GW contracted large load, and the nuclear uprate announcement with Google.
GS rates SO Neutral with a 12-month price target of $101, based on 19.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates. Price was $93.12 at the 4 Nov 2026 close, implying 8.5% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Neutral and the $101 target after the Q3 beat and the guidance raise. It cites regulatory and political risk after the Georgia election results.

sector_views.rationale: GS is Neutral on SO. It is encouraged by earnings execution and large load growth but sees higher political and regulatory risk after the elections.

earnings_insights: SO adjusted 3Q26 EPS reported at $1.94 vs GS estimate $1.72 and FactSet consensus $1.71 (reported 11/5/2026 per the First Take dated 5 Nov 2026).
SO raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.70 from $4.50-$4.60. GS estimate before the update was $4.63. The 8%-9% adjusted EPS growth guidance through 2028 was reiterated.
3Q26 adjusted net income was $2,242mn actual vs GS estimate $1,952mn, +15%. Total operating revenue was $8,852mn actual vs GSe $8,166mn.
Segment EPS actual vs GSe: Alabama Power $0.57 vs $0.53, Georgia Power $1.32 vs $1.23, Mississippi $0.08 vs $0.07, SO Gas $0.02 vs $0.01, Southern Power $0.12 vs $0.09, Parent ($0.18) vs ($0.21).
GS forecasts SO EPS of $4.65 for 2026E, $4.99 for 2027E and $5.40 for 2028E. GS forecasts 4Q26E EPS of $0.47 and 1Q27E EPS of $1.31.
SO is expected to refresh the $81bn capital plan in Q4, which could add capex beyond the $4bn already identified.
risk_factors: Negative developments on the regulatory front after the Georgia election results.
Possible revisions to load growth and the balance sheet.
Risk to the 75 GW+ prospective large load pipeline from regulatory and policy changes.
Net debt/EBITDA of 5.9x in 2026E and 2027E per GS forecasts, with negative FCF yield.
geopolitical: Georgia election results from earlier in the week are cited as raising political and regulatory risk for SO.
